correctness.rationale: For the given origin-incidence coisometry and phased flip, the determinant lemma and (zI+S)^(-1)S=(zS-I)/(z²-1) yield the full polynomial spectral map including the (z²-1)^(mn-m-n) factor. The off-diagonal m-by-n block B has one special row and all remaining rows equal. The squared singular-value sum is mn before normalization, and the product is (m−1)(n²−|n−1+e^(iβ)|²)=4(m−1)(n−1)sin²(β/2). Writing the normalized pair as cos θ, sin θ yields discriminant eigenvalues ±cos θ, ±sin θ and zeros, thus the mobile quartets i^j e^(±iθ). The proof's rank-two heading refers to B: the full Hermitian Q has rank four at nontrivial phase, rank two at zero phase. The displayed proof correctly uses all four discriminant modes. Unitarity makes the four-step defect rank and norm computations valid even at eigenvalue collisions. The ratio i forces a full period to be 4k; q|2k gives the claimed minimum. At zero flux θ=0 and the period is four. At the K_(2,2), β=π collision, θ=π/4 and all eight arc modes acquire fourth power −1. Strict monotonicity on either half-cycle gives the dense countable null exact-period set, and irrational rotation modulo π gives arbitrary norm revivals. Independent direct constructions gave (z^4+1)^2 and U^4=−I for K_(2,2) at π, and (z²−1)(z²+1)(z^8−(2/9)z^4+1) with defect singular values 4/3 eightfold for K_(2,3) at π/2; the K_(3,4) replay was numerical. The supplied verifier's recorded run was not an independent replay.
